name: Elena Vasquez
bio:
## About

Database engineer. I spent six years on the storage team at a payments company, which is a polite way of saying I spent six years being paged at 3am about replication lag.

### What I write about
- Postgres internals, mostly the parts that surprise people
- Query planning and why your index isn't being used
- Migrations that don't take the site down

> If your migration doesn't have a rollback plan, it isn't a migration. It's a bet.

name: Tomas Lindqvist
bio:
## Hej

Frontend architect in Stockholm. I care a lot about the boring parts of the browser — layout, paint, and the 200ms nobody can account for.

### Current obsessions
- View transitions and what they replace
- CSS container queries in real design systems
- Getting Lighthouse scores honestly instead of gaming them

Previously built design systems at two companies you've heard of and one you haven't.

name: Priya Raghunathan
bio:
## Background

Distributed systems, mostly. I like problems where the answer is "it depends on your consistency model."

### Focus
- Event-driven architectures that don't become event-driven spaghetti
- Idempotency as a design constraint, not an afterthought
- Observability: traces over logs, always

*Currently writing a book about failure modes that I will probably never finish.*

name: Marcus Bell
bio:
## Who I am

Self-taught, started in support, ended up in platform engineering. The support years were the most useful engineering education I got.

### Topics
1. Developer experience as a product discipline
2. Internal tooling nobody wants to own
3. Career paths that aren't management

I write about the parts of the job that don't fit in a commit message.

name: Yuki Tanaka
bio:
## Profile

Compiler and tooling work. I build the things that run before your code runs.

### Interests
- Incremental compilation and why builds get slow
- TypeScript's type system as a programming language in its own right
- Rust, WebAssembly, and the parts of both that are oversold

> Fast feedback loops are worth more than any individual optimization.

name: Aisha Okonkwo
bio:
## Hello

Security engineer with a background in application development, which means I break things I used to build.

### What I cover
- Threat modelling for teams that have never done it
- Auth flows: the ten ways OAuth goes wrong in practice
- Secrets management beyond "put it in the env file"

I believe most security incidents are design problems wearing a costume.

name: Daniel Roth
bio:
## Intro

Backend engineer, currently working on API design at a mid-size SaaS company.

### Writing about
- REST vs. RPC arguments that are actually about coupling
- Versioning strategies and their long-term costs
- Pagination, filtering, and other things everyone reinvents badly

I have strong opinions about error responses and I will share them.

name: Sofia Marchetti
bio:
## Chi sono

Design engineer working between the design and frontend teams — the seam where most product quality is won or lost.

### Areas
- Design tokens and the tooling that keeps them honest
- Accessibility as a default, not an audit finding
- Motion design that survives contact with real data

Based in Milan. Formerly agency, now product.

name: Jonas Weber
bio:
## About me

Infrastructure. Kubernetes when it's warranted, a single server when it isn't — and it usually isn't.

### Themes
- Cost as an architectural constraint
- Deployment pipelines that fail loudly and early
- The operational overhead nobody budgets for

> Every abstraction you adopt is an abstraction you have to debug at 2am.

name: Nadia Haddad
bio:
## Bio

Data engineer turned analytics lead. I moved from building pipelines to arguing about what the numbers mean, which is harder.

### Subjects
- Modelling events so they're still useful in a year
- Warehouse costs and the queries that drive them
- Metrics that change behaviour vs. metrics that decorate dashboards

name: Oliver Grant
bio:
## Hi

Staff engineer, currently doing a lot of migration work — the kind that takes eighteen months and has no demo.

### I write about
- Strangler-fig migrations and when to abandon them
- Legacy code as an asset rather than a liability
- Technical debt conversations with non-technical stakeholders

Ten years in, still mostly deleting code.

name: Camila Duarte
bio:
## Sobre

Mobile engineer working across React Native and native iOS. I've shipped the same feature three times in three frameworks and have opinions about it.

### Focus areas
- Cross-platform tradeoffs, honestly assessed
- Offline-first sync and conflict resolution
- App performance on the devices people actually own

Based in São Paulo.

name: Henrik Solberg
bio:
## Background

Testing and quality engineering. I got here by being the person who kept asking why the suite was red.

### Writing on
- Test pyramids and why yours is an hourglass
- Flaky tests as a systems problem
- Contract testing between services

> A test suite you don't trust is worse than no test suite. It costs the same and tells you nothing.

name: Leila Farsi
bio:
## About

Engineering manager, formerly a backend developer who missed writing code and now writes about not writing code.

### Topics
- Team topologies and cognitive load
- Hiring processes that don't filter for interview skill
- Incident review without blame theatre

I manage six people and read a great deal about managing six people.

name: Andrei Popescu
bio:
## Hello

Performance engineer. My job is mostly measuring things carefully and then telling people their assumptions were wrong.

### Areas
- Profiling methodology, and why flame graphs mislead
- Latency budgets across a request path
- Caching strategies and their invalidation costs

*Measure first. Then measure again, differently.*

name: Grace Whitfield
bio:
## Intro

Technical writer who codes, or a developer who writes — the ratio shifts by quarter.

### Subjects
- Documentation as part of the product surface
- API reference generation from source
- Onboarding paths that get someone to a working call in five minutes

I think most docs problems are actually information architecture problems.

name: Rafael Ortiz
bio:
## Sobre mí

Full-stack developer at a small team where everyone touches everything. Generalist by necessity, which turned out to suit me.

### What I cover
- Small-team architecture decisions
- Choosing boring technology on purpose
- Shipping with two engineers and no platform team

Based in Mexico City.

name: Ingrid Nilsen
bio:
## About

Product engineer with a research background. I spend a lot of time on the question of whether we should build the thing at all.

### Interests
- Prototyping to answer questions, not to impress
- Feature flags and progressive delivery
- Instrumenting a feature before shipping it

> The cheapest feature is the one you proved you didn't need.

name: Kwame Mensah
bio:
## Hi there

Open-source maintainer and infrastructure developer. I maintain two libraries, one of which people actually use.

### Writing about
- Maintainer burnout and issue triage at scale
- Semantic versioning as a social contract
- Dependency risk in modern package ecosystems

Most of my best code was written in response to someone else's bug report.

name: Mei Lin Chow
bio:
## Profile

Machine learning engineer working on retrieval systems. Less model training than people expect, more data plumbing.

### Focus
- Evaluation sets and why yours is leaking
- Retrieval quality as an engineering problem
- Serving latency for model-backed features

I am suspicious of any benchmark I did not build myself.
